subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: World Religions Judaism Islam Buddhism Hinduism
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is 'samsara' in Hinduism?
options: The cycle of birth, death and rebirth
questions.explain: Samsara is the continuous cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

questions.q: Muslims believe that Jannah and Jahannam refer to:
options: Paradise and Hell in the afterlife
questions.explain: Jannah is Paradise and Jahannam is Hell, the two destinations after the Day of Judgement.

questions.q: In the Theravada tradition, the ideal figure to aspire to is the:
options: Bodhisattva who delays nirvana to help others
questions.explain: In Theravada Buddhism the ideal is the arhat, one who achieves enlightenment and escapes rebirth.

questions.q: Al-Qadr in Islam refers to:
options: God's predestination and the idea that he knows all that will happen
questions.explain: Al-Qadr is the belief in predestination, that God has knowledge of and decrees all events.

questions.q: Muslims describe Allah as 'transcendent', meaning that God is:
options: Beyond and above his creation, not part of it
questions.explain: Transcendence means God is beyond and above creation, not contained within the material world.

questions.q: What is 'moksha' in Hindu belief?
options: Liberation from the cycle of rebirth
The law of cause and effect
questions.explain: Moksha is release or liberation from samsara, the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.

questions.q: On the Day of Judgement, Muslims believe people will be:
options: Judged by God on their deeds and sent to Paradise or Hell
questions.explain: Muslims believe God will judge each person by their actions, leading to Paradise or Hell.

questions.q: Vipassana meditation is mainly concerned with developing:
options: Insight into the true nature of reality
questions.explain: Vipassana meditation develops insight into the true nature of reality, such as impermanence.

questions.q: The Dhamma (Dharma), one of the Three Refuges, refers to:
options: The Buddhist community of monks and nuns
questions.explain: The Dhamma is the teachings of the Buddha, one of the Three Refuges alongside the Buddha and the Sangha.

questions.q: In Islam, Muhammad is regarded as:
options: The final prophet (the Seal of the Prophets)
questions.explain: Muslims believe Muhammad is the last and final prophet, the Seal of the Prophets.

questions.q: Malaikah in Islam are:
options: Angels who serve and obey God
questions.explain: Malaikah are angels, beings created by God who carry out his commands, such as Jibril.

questions.q: The Arabic phrase 'subhanahu wa ta'ala', often said after Allah's name, expresses:
questions.explain: This phrase means 'glorified and exalted is he', showing reverence when Muslims mention God.

questions.q: In Mahayana Buddhism, a bodhisattva is someone who:
options: Rules as a king over a Buddhist land
Delays their own nirvana to help others reach enlightenment
Rejects the teachings of the Buddha
questions.explain: In Mahayana Buddhism a bodhisattva compassionately delays final nirvana to help others reach enlightenment.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four aims of life (Purusharthas)?
questions.explain: Moksha (liberation) is one of the four aims of life, with dharma, artha and kama.

questions.q: Which of these is a factor of the Eightfold Path?
questions.explain: Right intention is one of the eight factors of the Eightfold Path, the way to end suffering.

questions.q: Belief in Tawhid means Muslims reject:
options: Associating any partners or equals with God (shirk)
questions.explain: Because God is one, Muslims reject shirk, the sin of associating partners with God.

questions.q: What do many Hindus believe about the relationship between the atman and Brahman?
options: That there are many separate eternal souls and no Brahman
That atman is part of, and ultimately one with, Brahman
That the soul is destroyed at death
questions.explain: Many Hindus believe the atman (inner self) is part of, and ultimately one with, Brahman.

questions.q: Before reaching enlightenment, Siddhartha first tried which approach to find the truth?
options: A life of severe self-denial and extreme asceticism
Worshipping many gods at a temple
questions.explain: Siddhartha first practised extreme asceticism but found it did not lead to truth, so he chose the Middle Way.

questions.q: Diwali in many traditions recalls the return of which figure after defeating the demon Ravana?
questions.explain: Diwali often celebrates the return of Rama to Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana.

questions.q: Which path to moksha emphasises selfless action and duty without attachment to results?
questions.explain: Karma yoga is the path to moksha through selfless action and performing one's duty without attachment.

questions.q: What is a 'murti' in Hindu worship?
options: A sacred image or statue of a deity
questions.explain: A murti is a sacred image or statue of a deity used as a focus for worship in puja.

questions.q: The three sections of the Eightfold Path are wisdom, meditation and:
questions.explain: The Eightfold Path is grouped into wisdom, ethics (morality) and meditation.
